question: What condition does the entire world appear to have assumed after the slaughter?
premises: The entirety is described as having become something.
That state is characterized as being about to die.
This condition is presented as an appearance or semblance.
inference: The whole world appears to have entered a state resembling imminent death.
uncertainties: The exact referent of sakalaṃ as the whole world or all things is inferred from context.
plain_english: Everything appears to have become as if about to die.
